title: Never Headed: Neumann's Long Climb Ends at Estoril
title_candidates: Never Headed: Neumann's Long Climb Ends at Estoril
Two Spoons and a Trophy: Neumann Leads All the Way
The Man Who Led Every Round
Records Fall at Estoril, But Nobody Moves
theme: Nothing moved and everything changed: Stuart Neumann led the TEG 16 Trophy from the first evening to the last, Gregg Williams led the Jacket the same way, Alex Baker was bottom after all four rounds — and the only genuine drama was in the record books at Estoril, where the lowest and highest gross scores TEG has recorded there were both posted on the same afternoon.
opening_hook: Open on Stuart Neumann's back catalogue — two Wooden Spoons, no Trophy, and four TEGs of patient climbing (6th, 5th, 3rd, 2nd) — then cut to the one fact that settled TEG 16: he led after R1 and was never headed. Career-first framing, because the result itself had no suspense in it.

trophy_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann, twice a Spoon holder and never a champion, leads the TEG 16 Trophy wire to wire and wins by 13
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: Neumann arrived with 2 prior Wooden Spoons and no Trophy wins, having finished 6th, 5th, 3rd and 2nd across his last four TEGs; this is the first win of his TEG career.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: 39 points at Oitavos Dunes on day one put him 5 clear, and the Trophy lead never left him after that (b08, b28, b43) — best in the field in each of the first three rounds, and ahead of Gregg Williams in all four. Turn: R3 at Penha Longa, another 39, and the cushion went from 7 to 12 while the rest of the field was busy losing shots in threes and fours. Resolution: 43 points at Estoril in R4, a 92 gross that was 14 better than his TEG 15 visit there, and he managed it while posting a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 8th, the hardest hole on the course (b46) — 156 points, 13 clear (b01).
headline_candidates: Two Spoons, Then This: Neumann Wins by 13
Neumann Leads From Oitavos and Is Never Caught
One Trophy at Last, and He Led Throughout
trophy_storyline.chosen_headline: Two Spoons, Then This: Neumann Wins by 13
trophy_storyline.standfirst: The only man in the field without a Trophy to his name led after every round of TEG 16 and finished ahead of the defending champion, Gregg Williams, in all four.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams retains the Green Jacket with the lowest gross total of his TEG career, pulling 16 clear of David Mullin
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Williams was the gross leader after every round and finished at +66, the best gross total he has recorded in a TEG, adding a second Jacket to the one he won at TEG 15.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: 89 gross at Oitavos Dunes, a personal best there by 2, gave him a lead of only 3, and Troia kept it tight — Jon Baker drew level twice in R2 while Williams went four holes without a net par from the 8th (b41) and dropped six shots from the 13th (b48, b50). Turn: Penha Longa in R3, where a triple at the 3rd and a double at the 4th were stopped dead by a birdie at the 5th (b25), then five holes without dropping a gross shot from the 11th (b18) and nine points from the 13th (b23); the margin went from 4 to 14. Resolution: R4 at Estoril was administration — nine points from the 6th (b11, b16) before the run ended with a double at the 9th (b06) and a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 14th (b03) that cost him nothing at all (b02).
headline_candidates: Williams Breaks It Open at Penha Longa
Sixteen Clear: Williams Keeps the Green Jacket
Five Clean Holes Settle the Jacket
jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: Williams Breaks It Open at Penha Longa
jacket_storyline.standfirst: Four shots up going into R3 and sixteen up at the finish: the defending Jacket holder's +66 is the lowest gross he has posted in a TEG, and David Mullin was never close enough to ask a question.

spoon_storyline.subject: Alex Baker takes a second consecutive Wooden Spoon and sets course-worst records at both Oitavos Dunes and Estoril on the way
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: He came in as the reigning Spoon holder from TEG 15 and leaves with his third, bottom of the Trophy table after every single round on 127 points.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 1st at Oitavos Dunes (b49) set the terms, another 9 followed at the 11th (b47) and a sextuple-bogey 10 at the 17th (b37) closed a 113 — the worst gross TEG has ever recorded at Oitavos Dunes, across 12 prior visits (cr03). Turn: he took ownership of the Spoon race for good on the 13th at Troia, in the middle of a five-hole stretch that cost 13 shots (b33), and in fairness his scoring improved every round — 29, 32, 33, 33 — which is the sort of steadiness nobody wants credited to them. Resolution: Estoril in R4, where he opened with a 9 (b32), added an 8 at the 3rd (b39) and a 9 at the 6th (b38), bled 14 shots between the 5th and the 10th (b30, b31) and then ran up a septuple-bogey 11 at the 12th (b09), the worst hole relative to par of his TEG career; the 107 is a new Estoril course-worst (cr02) and the Spoon was his by 4 (b24).
headline_candidates: Two Course Records, Both the Wrong Way
Back-to-Back Spoons, and an Eleven at Estoril
spoon_storyline.chosen_headline: Two Course Records, Both the Wrong Way
spoon_storyline.standfirst: Alex Baker was bottom of the TEG 16 Trophy table after all four rounds, and left Oitavos Dunes and Estoril with higher gross scores than TEG has ever recorded at either.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin answers a wrecked Penha Longa round with an 80 at Estoril, the lowest gross TEG has recorded on the course
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Mullin, with 9 prior Jacket wins, was 13 shots worse at Penha Longa than on his previous visit and then broke the Estoril course record the following day — the single best round of the tournament, arriving with nothing left to play for.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 at Oitavos Dunes had already had him briefly bottom of the Spoon race after a triple at the 10th (b40), and R3 at Penha Longa was worse — 98 gross, 30 points, and a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 16th, the hardest hole on the card (b05). Turn: at Estoril he was 2 under par through the 3rd (b22), stopped a run of bogeys with a birdie at the 7th (b04), then took nine points from the 11th to the 13th (b07, b14) and parred the 16th and 17th to keep it clean (b10). Resolution: an 80, beating the prior Estoril best of 86 across 6 prior visits (cr01), 14 better than his own TEG 15 mark there, and a 15-point swing on his own previous round (b13) — by which time the Jacket had been Gregg Williams's for a day.
headline_candidates: Mullin's 80 Is the Lowest Estoril Has Seen
Ninety-Eight, Then Eighty: Mullin's Sharp Turn
A Course Record With Nothing Riding On It
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Mullin's 80 Is the Lowest Estoril Has Seen
discovered_storylines.standfirst: The nine-time Jacket winner was 13 shots worse at Penha Longa than on his last visit, then took 18 fewer strokes the very next day.

discovered_storylines.subject: Both Baker brothers come apart on the same stretch of Penha Longa's back nine, sharing a 10 and a 9 at the 12th
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Jon Baker and Alex Baker are brothers, and in R3 they lost 11 and 12 shots respectively over near-identical holes, with most of the damage done by the 12th — stroke index 17, one of the easiest holes on the course.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: both reached the turn at Penha Longa intact enough, Jon Baker having been level with the Jacket lead only a round earlier at Troia. Turn: from the 11th Jon Baker went double, quintuple, quadruple — a 10 at the 12th (b34) and an 8 at the 13th (b42), 11 shots gone in three holes and not a net par among them (b21, b27); Alex Baker matched the choreography with a 9 at the same 12th (b44) and triples at the 13th and 14th, 12 shots in four (b19, b26). Resolution: Jon Baker finished 12 shots worse at Penha Longa than on his last visit, carried the habit to Estoril with a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 11th, the second-hardest hole there (b36), and still posted his best Estoril round, 93.
headline_candidates: The Bakers Both Break at the Twelfth
A Ten and a Nine, Same Hole
Brothers Undone by Penha Longa's Easy Par Five
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: The Bakers Both Break at the Twelfth
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Penha Longa's 12th is stroke index 17, one of the easiest holes on the card; in R3 it took a 10 off Jon Baker and a 9 off Alex Baker, and neither brother made a net par anywhere near it.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as a supporting vehicle: Alex Baker's seven blow-ups and two course-worsts make the Spoon a genuine inventory of failure. It doesn't frame the report, because the week belongs to Stuart Neumann's first Trophy after two Spoons.

why_the_champion_won: Neumann built it rather than inherited it: best in the field in each of the first three rounds, ahead of Gregg Williams head-to-head in all four, and the lead grew every round from 5 to 13 — Williams playing to his own average instead of his worst round would still have lost.
